title: Grateful Dead Live at Century II Convention Hall on 1972-11-17
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CR > EAC > WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy Wichita ‘72 show captured on a soundboard with generally clear audio (despite occasional noise‑reduction patches), highlighted by scorching “Cumberland Blues”, “He’s Gone”, “The Other One” and a soaring “Bird Song”.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers one of the standout performances from the fall‑1972 tour – Jerry’s ferocious lead on Cumberland and He’s Gone, Phil’s bass‑line fireworks on The Other One, and a rare, fire‑breathing Bird Song.  The SBD source is mostly crisp; a few murky patches, speed quirks and splice gaps are noted but do not detract from the overall listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently enthusiastic comments about the musical performance (≈4.5/5) and generally good soundboard quality with only minor technical flaws (≈3.8/5) yield a weighted average of ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mostly crisp and clear SBD; some reviewers note a 30‑second murky patch, occasional noise‑reduction artifacts, minor static/splices and slight speed issues that require pitch correction.

standout_songs: Truckin’ > The Other One > Brokedown Palace
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds with strong openings (China>Rider, Bird Song) and rare Box of Rain; second set launches with a blistering Cumberland Blues leading into an epic He’s Gone → Truckin’ → The Other One jam sequence, ending smoothly with Brokedown Palace.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for ferocious, original playing; “underwater” filter tone on Cumberland; superb leads on He’s Gone and The Other One; overall guitar work described as scorching and inventive.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “Miles Davis Footprints”‑style bass lines; strong, melodic support during The Other One; occasional “bass bombs” that drive the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Recognized for rhythmic brilliance on Sugaree and other cuts; some reviewers call his rhythm bordering on a second lead; highlighted as original rhythm guitarist.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s jazz‑inflected improvisation (Round Midnight reference) and tight interplay with Jerry noted; praised for finding his way and adding texture throughout the set.
